blk_part_01_who_the_greek_gods_were.text: Because the gods had human feelings, the Greeks believed they could please them with gifts. The most important gift was a sacrifice: people killed an animal on an altar, a stone table for gifts. The altar stood outside, in front of the temple. The temple was the house of the god, and a statue of the god stood inside. In a sacrifice, people burned the bones and fat for the god. Then they cooked the meat and ate it together. Meat was expensive, so many Greeks rarely ate it except at festivals for the gods.

blk_part_02_zeus_king_of_the_sky.text: His most famous story explains how he became king. His father, Cronus, ruled the world before him. Cronus was afraid that one of his children would take his power. So every time his wife Rhea had a baby, he swallowed it whole. When Zeus was born, Rhea had a plan. She wrapped a stone in baby clothes and gave it to Cronus. He swallowed the stone without noticing. The real baby grew up in secret on the island of Crete. When Zeus was an adult, he forced his father to throw up his brothers and sisters, still alive. Together they fought Cronus and won. The story shows the character of Zeus: clever, strong and ready to fight for power.

Travelling was slow and dangerous, so a traveller often depended on the kindness of strangers. Zeus turned that kindness into a duty.

They believed he caused earthquakes by hitting the ground with his trident. Greece has many earthquakes, and it has sea on three sides and thousands of islands. Sailors gave gifts to Poseidon and asked him to protect them. For them, a calm sea meant life, and a storm meant death. At Sounion, on a cliff south-east of Athens, his temple still stands above the water. Ships on their way to Athens could see it.

blk_part_03_poseidon_god_of_the_sea.text: His most famous story shows that Poseidon did not easily forgive anyone who hurt his family. In the Odyssey, a famous Greek poem, the hero Odysseus is going home after a long war. On an island, a giant with one eye traps him and his men in a cave. The giant, Polyphemus, begins to eat them. Odysseus escapes by blinding the giant. But Polyphemus is the son of Poseidon. The angry god sends storms, and Odysseus wanders the sea for ten years before he gets home. For the Greeks, the message was clear. The sea is powerful, it does not forget, and you must respect it.

Her bird was the owl, and the Greeks connected owls with wisdom.

Poseidon hit a rock with his trident, and water came out. But it was salt water, like the sea. The people could not drink it or use it on their fields. Athena made an olive tree grow. The people chose her gift, and the city took her name: Athens.
